sd1.intro: The Classical foundation: Black takes on c4, develops the light-squared bishop, and a knight comes to a6 against White's knight on e5.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the diagonal open for the light-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and supports the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4. Black accepts it for the moment so the light-squared bishop can come out.
a4 stops a queenside pawn rush and fixes the pawn on c4.
Bf5 develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain, which is why Black took on c4.
Ne5 plants the knight in the centre and attacks the pawn on c6.
Na6 develops the queen's knight. The pawn on c6 has taken its natural square, so the knight uses the edge.

sd2.intro: The Classical with safe development: White takes the pawn back, and Black pins with the bishop before both sides castle.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the diagonal open for the light-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and supports the centre.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4 so the light-squared bishop can develop.
a4 stops a queenside pawn rush before White takes the pawn back.
Bf5 develops the light-squared bishop to an active square.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
e6 supports the centre. The light-squared bishop is already outside the chain, so this pawn does not shut it in.
Bxc4 takes the pawn on c4 and develops the light-squared bishop. White wins the offered pawn back.
Bb4 pins the knight on c3 to the king on e1.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. The king steps off the pin.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king steps off the e-file.

sd3.intro: The Czech Slav: White's knight takes the light-squared bishop, and Black takes back with the e-pawn. Black then develops the dark-squared bishop, castles, and puts a knight on d7.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the diagonal open for the light-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4 so the light-squared bishop can develop.
a4 stops a queenside pawn rush.
Bf5 develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain.
Nh4 attacks the bishop on f5. White would rather take this bishop than let it sit.
e6 supports the centre and prepares to recapture on f5.
Nxf5 takes the bishop on f5. White gives a knight for the light-squared bishop.
exf5 recaptures the knight on f5. The e-file opens and the f-pawns are doubled.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
Bd6 develops the dark-squared bishop and attacks the pawn on h2. The bishop takes an active diagonal before Black castles.
Bxc4 takes the pawn on c4 and attacks the pawn on f7. White wins the offered pawn back.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king steps off the e-file.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. White's king leaves the centre as well.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the knight on f6. The knight also stands beside the rook on f8.
Qc2 develops the queen and attacks the pawn on f5. The doubled pawns on the f-file are the target.
g6 defends the pawn on f5 and gives the king on g8 a little room. Black does not push that pawn any further yet.

sd4.intro: White leaves out the a-pawn. Black holds the pawn with the b-pawn, and the knight is driven off c3 before White takes on c4.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the diagonal open for the light-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4. White has not restrained the queenside, so Black can try to keep the pawn.
e3 supports the centre and prepares to take the pawn back.
b5 holds the pawn on c4 and gains queenside space.
a4 attacks the pawn on b5 and challenges that space.
b4 attacks the knight on c3 and gains more space.
Na2 steps the knight off the pawn. The edge is an awkward square, which is the cost of omitting the earlier restraint.
e6 supports the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
Bxc4 takes the pawn on c4. White gets the pawn back after all.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the pawn on b4. It also defends the knight on f6, so Black can castle.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. White castles before Black does.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. Both kings are safe, and Black still has the queenside space.
b3 supports the bishop on c4 and the pawn on a4. It also frees the dark-squared bishop.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the knight on f6. The knight also defends the rook on f8.
Bb2 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the pawn on d4. The bishop takes the long diagonal.
Bb7 develops the light-squared bishop behind the pawn on c6. It defends that pawn and the rook on a8, and it can wait until the centre opens.

sd5.intro: The Slow Slav: White plays the e-pawn before the queen's knight, the light-squared bishops are traded, and Black castles with the queen on c7.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the diagonal open for the light-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop. White is in no hurry to attack d5 with a knight.
Bf5 develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
e6 supports the centre. The light-squared bishop is already out.
Bd3 challenges the bishop on f5. White offers a trade of light-squared bishops.
Bxd3 takes the bishop on d3. Black accepts the trade of light-squared bishops that White offered.
Qxd3 recaptures the bishop on d3 and attacks the pawn on h7. The queen replaces the bishop on that square.
Be7 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on f6.
O-O brings the king to g1 and the rook to f1. White castles before Black's knight arrives.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the knight on f6.
b3 supports the pawn on c4 and frees the dark-squared bishop. That bishop can use b2.
O-O brings the king to g8 and the rook to f8. The king steps off the e-file.
Bb2 develops the dark-squared bishop and defends the knight on c3.
Qc7 develops the queen and attacks the pawn on h2. The queen also defends the knight on d7 and the pawn on c6.

sd6.intro: The Slow Slav with the bishop dropping back: White takes it, Black takes back, and the dark-squared bishop comes to d6.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the diagonal open for the light-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
Bf5 develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
e6 supports the centre.
Nh4 attacks the bishop on f5.
Bg6 steps the bishop off the knight and stays on the same diagonal.
Nxg6 takes the bishop on g6. White removes the light-squared bishop.
hxg6 recaptures the knight on g6 and opens the h-file.
g3 prepares a fianchetto. The light-squared bishop will sit on the long diagonal.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and defends the knight on f6.
Bg2 puts the light-squared bishop on the long diagonal.
Bd6 develops the dark-squared bishop and aims towards the kingside.

sd7.intro: The Exchange: the c-pawns come off, and both sides develop the remaining pieces to natural squares.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the diagonal open for the light-squared bishop.
cxd5 takes the pawn on d5 and attacks the pawn on c6.
cxd5 recaptures the pawn on d5. The c-file is open, and the structure is symmetrical.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
Nc6 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d4.
Bf4 develops the dark-squared bishop to an active square.
Bf5 develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain, matching the active bishop White just developed.

sd8.intro: The Exchange with queen pressure: White's queen comes to b3, and Black's queen defends from c7.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the diagonal open for the light-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
Bf5 develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain.
cxd5 takes the pawn on d5 and opens the c-file.
cxd5 recaptures the pawn on d5. The c-file is open.
Qb3 develops the queen and attacks the pawn on b7 and the pawn on d5.
Qc7 develops the queen, defends the pawn on b7, and keeps an eye on the open c-file.

sd9.intro: The Chebanenko: Black plays the a-pawn instead of taking on c4, White pushes the c-pawn, and a knight comes to h5 against the dark-squared bishop.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the diagonal open for the light-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
a6 is the Chebanenko move. It prepares queenside expansion and keeps a white piece off b5.
c5 gains space and clamps the queenside. White does not wait for Black to expand.
Bf5 develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain.
Bf4 develops the dark-squared bishop to an active square.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and supports a later central break.
e3 supports the centre and frees the light-squared bishop.
Nh5 attacks the bishop on f4 and offers a trade of that bishop.

sd10.intro: Central counterplay: Black develops against the knight on e5, the queen comes to c7, and the e-pawn breaks in the centre.
notes: d4 claims the centre and frees the dark-squared bishop.
d5 meets White in the centre.
c4 offers a pawn to fight for d5.
c6 supports the pawn on d5 and leaves the diagonal open for the light-squared bishop.
Nf3 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d4.
Nf6 develops the king's knight and defends the pawn on d5.
Nc3 develops the queen's knight and attacks the pawn on d5.
dxc4 takes the pawn on c4 so the light-squared bishop can develop.
a4 stops a queenside pawn rush.
Bf5 develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain.
Ne5 plants the knight in the centre and attacks the pawn on c6.
Nbd7 develops the queen's knight and attacks the central knight.
Nxc4 takes the pawn on c4 and steps the knight off the attack.
Qc7 develops the queen and defends the pawn on c6.
g3 prepares a fianchetto.
e5 breaks in the centre and attacks the pawn on d4. This is the counterplay the line is built on.
